details: A memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran has been finalized and is set for signing on June 19 in Switzerland. The agreement includes lifting naval blockades and opening the Strait of Hormuz. Bitcoin (BTC) responded by climbing 2.48% to $65,642.70, while Ethereum (ETH) increased 3.65% to $1,723.88. Further negotiations on sanctions and nuclear issues are planned within 60 days.
title: US-Iran Deal Confirmed, Bitcoin Rises 2.48%

details: Bitcoin's mining difficulty saw a significant 10.09% drop on June 14, marking the second-largest negative adjustment in 2026. This recalibration is a response to reduced hashrate and falling Bitcoin prices (down about 15% in June), easing the operational burden and potentially improving profitability for active miners.
title: Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Drops 10% Amid Miner Pressure

details: Zimbabwe has rolled out new regulations requiring cryptocurrency firms to register annually with the central bank's Financial Intelligence Unit. This move aims to formalize the digital asset industry and enhance oversight, with an initial registration fee of $500 and annual renewals at $400.
title: Zimbabwe Moves to Regulate Crypto Sector, Firms Must Register

details: The cryptocurrency derivatives market experienced $303 million in futures liquidations over the past 24 hours. Bitcoin (BTC) accounted for $92.16 million of these liquidations, followed by Ethereum (ETH) with $64.84 million, indicating significant volatility and risk for leveraged positions.
title: Crypto Futures See $303 Million Liquidations in 24 Hours

details: Poland has issued its third veto against the country's crypto bill, which further postpones the adoption of the Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation across the European Union. This prolongs regulatory uncertainty for crypto firms seeking EU market access and could lead to potential business relocations.
title: Poland's Veto Delays EU MiCA Crypto Regulation Adoption
